core_obligations: Reduce to normal surfaces (proof lines 1296-1304): replace the source by its normalization and factor the morphism through the normalization of the target, so that both are normal; then the morphism is an isomorphism outside a finite set of closed points T of the target.

Set up the induction on bad curves (proof lines 1306-1330): over each bad point the fibre is proper, geometrically connected of dimension one, so the set of closed curves contracted by the morphism is finite; the proof proceeds by induction on the number of these curves, the base case being the situation where the morphism is an isomorphism.

Compare the bad curves along the normalized blowup of a bad point (proof lines 1332-1336): let X' be the normalized blowup at a bad point and Y' the normalization of the base change; a bad curve in Y' maps to an irreducible component of the corresponding fibre in Y and is determined by it, because the morphism Y' to Y is an isomorphism over points of codimension one, so one obtains an injection from the bad curves of the new morphism into those of the old one and it suffices to kill at least one of them.

Kill one bad curve by Zariski's argument (proof lines 1338-1384): choose a bad curve C and an element of the local ring of the target at its generic point whose image in the residue field of C is transcendental over the residue field of the bad point; writing it as a quotient of elements of the local ring at the bad point, both numerator and denominator must lie in the maximal ideal, and the minimum of their orders along C is a positive integer; after the normalized blowup, the exceptional divisor provides a common factor d so that the corresponding numerator and denominator of the new situation have strictly smaller orders along the lifted curve, so a descending induction on that integer shows that after finitely many normalized blowups at closed points at least one bad curve disappears, which completes the induction.
proof_roadmap: Normalize both schemes so that the morphism is an isomorphism outside finitely many closed points.
Count the contracted curves and run an induction on their number, comparing them along a normalized blowup of a bad point.
Kill one contracted curve using Zariski's local computation with the orders of a transcendental residue class, via descending induction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a proper birational morphism towards a two dimensional Noetherian Nagata scheme is dominated by the normalization followed by a finite sequence of normalized blowups at closed points (statement lines 1276-1294). The proof (proof lines 1296-1387) reduces to normal surfaces, shows that only finitely many curves are contracted, runs an induction on their number comparing the contracted curves along a normalized blowup, and kills one of them by Zariski's argument computing orders of a transcendental residue class along the lifted curve, concluding by descending induction. H3: a substantial induction with an original local computation, written out in full.
